stem: An urban planning study measures the commute time (minutes) for a sample of 20 city workers. The sample mean is 36.8 min with a sample standard deviation of 12.6 min. However, 2 of the 20 observations appear to be outliers (values more than 2.5 standard deviations from the mean). If these outliers are removed, the remaining 18 observations have a mean of 36.0 min and standard deviation of 8.2 min. Estimate the true population mean and provide a 95% confidence interval that accounts for the uncertainty about whether outliers should be included.

ground_truth.answer: With all data: mean = 36.8, 95% CI = [30.9, 42.7]. Without outliers: mean = 36.0, 95% CI = [32.1, 39.9]. Combined interval accounting for analytic uncertainty: [30.9, 42.7]. Point estimate: 36.4 min.

solution_steps: The outlier treatment choice creates structural uncertainty. Combined interval: [30.9, 42.7].
common_failure_modes: Using only the full sample without considering outlier impact
Removing outliers without reporting both analyses
Not recognizing that the choice of analysis method is itself a source of uncertainty
